_note: Roster carried over from gawadlab.org (last updated 2022). VERIFY before publishing: move people who have left to 'alumni', add new members, and update titles. Images live in src/assets/people/.

current.name: Charles Gawad, MD, PhD
current.bio: Chuck is an Associate Professor of Pediatrics at Stanford Medicine and a practicing pediatric oncologist. He invented primary template-directed amplification (PTA) and co-founded BioSkryb Genomics. Outside of work he enjoys anything outdoors in the Bay Area and spending time with his family.

current.name: Veronica Gonzalez-Pena, PhD
current.bio: Veronica received her PhD in Pharmacology and Toxicology from the University of Arizona. In the lab she is passionate about working out the details of new biotechnology methods. In her free time she enjoys gardening and spending time with her family.

current.name: Yakun Pang, PhD
current.bio: Yakun received her PhD in Internal Medicine (Hematology) from Peking Union Medical College in 2016 and joined the lab in 2018. She studies pediatric acute leukemia with single-cell genomic and transcriptomic sequencing, with a focus on the mechanisms of leukemia development and treatment resistance.

current.name: Kartika Wardhani, PhD
current.bio: Kartika received her PhD in Chemistry from the University of Sydney. She is passionate about discoveries that advance science and human health, and about working with other researchers and students to solve big challenges. She loves traveling to meet local people and learn about new cultures.

current.name: David Klein
current.bio: David received a BA in Biology from NYU and an MS in Biomedical Sciences from Tufts, and is now a medical student at the California University of Science and Medicine. He is passionate about computational biology and creating new knowledge, tools, and therapies. He loves hiking, running, rock climbing, and backpacking.

current.name: Athena Aragon
current.bio: Athena joined the lab in 2021 after earning her bachelor's in Human Biology at UC Santa Cruz. She is interested in using single-cell sequencing to learn more about neurodegenerative diseases and pediatric leukemia. When she's not in lab, she plays guitar and discovers new places to eat.

current.name: Brandon Cai
current.bio: Brandon studied Molecular and Cell Biology and Public Health at UC Berkeley. He is passionate about single-cell data analysis, innovative thinking in research, and question-driven analysis. He loves listening to and making music, exploring nature, and playing basketball.

current.name: Shawn Schulz
current.bio: Shawn majored in Molecular and Cell Biology at UC Berkeley. He applies data science and computational analysis to medical research, contributing to personalized treatment of diseases like cancer using -omic data. He loves rock climbing, history, and tabletop games.

alumni.name: Syahmi Ali Mohd Rizal
alumni.bio: Stanford undergraduate in engineering who worked on emerging medical technologies in the lab.

alumni.name: Vibhu Agarwal, PhD
alumni.bio: Vibhu received his PhD in Biostatistics from Stanford. He developed the e-nose AI analytics in the lab before becoming Senior Director of Data Science at Medidata Solutions.

alumni.name: Yuntao Xia, PhD
alumni.bio: Yuntao received his PhD in Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering from UPenn. He developed single-cell and cell-free sequencing protocols and pipelines before becoming a Senior Scientist at Orchid Health.

alumni.name: Sivaraman Natarajan, PhD
alumni.bio: Siva received his PhD in Neuroscience from Universität des Saarlandes. He helped develop several new single-cell and cell-free DNA sequencing protocols before becoming a Staff Scientist at St. Jude.

alumni.name: Rob Carter, PhD
alumni.bio: Rob received his PhD in Biology from the University of Ottawa. He led the development of the lab's computational pipelines, then joined BioSkryb Genomics as Director of Bioinformatics.

alumni.name: Anju Cherian
alumni.bio: Anju received her MS in Biomedical Research from the Morehouse School of Medicine and worked on single-cell sequencing methods. She continued as a technician at St. Jude when the lab moved to Stanford.

alumni.name: Ousman Mahmud, PhD
alumni.bio: Ousman received his PhD in Genetics from the University of Georgia. He built computational pipelines for cell-free and single-cell sequencing before becoming a Genomics Bioinformatician at IBM Watson Health.

alumni.name: Yuki Inaba
alumni.bio: Yuki received a BS from Brown and worked on cell-free DNA sequencing before entering the MD/PhD program at UT Southwestern.

alumni.name: Morgan Carter
alumni.bio: Morgan developed methods for single-cell mitochondrial sequencing as an undergraduate at the University of Virginia, then received an NCI Cancer Research Training Award to continue at NIH.

alumni.name: Ian Nykaza
alumni.bio: Ian learned single-cell sequencing as an undergraduate at the University of Minnesota, worked as a clinical coordinator at UCSF, and entered medical school at Cornell.

alumni.name: Sarah Youssef
alumni.bio: Sarah completed her MS in Pharmacology as a Fulbright Scholar studying cell-free DNA sequencing, then returned to Cairo as a lead pharmacist at the Children's Cancer Hospital Egypt.

alumni.name: Greg Schwing
alumni.bio: Greg studied barcoding and single-cell sequencing of leukemia samples as an undergraduate at the University of New Orleans before entering the MD/PhD program at Wayne State University.

alumni.name: Shelby Lane
alumni.bio: Shelby studied single-cell sequencing of leukemia samples before starting medical school at the University of Tennessee Health Science Center.
